creator: Alexander Terp
description:
amterp, Chat Notes 2026-10-20: "right click split into daemon doesn't allow seamless pane placement like a same daemon pane would". At triage on 2026-10-21 he asked for the general form and called it high priority: any arrangement of panes in a tab, with the daemon a pane runs on having no effect on where it can go.

Today a tab holds one region per machine, side by side, and each region draws that machine's own split tree (docs/architecture.md: "The core owns composition" and "The arrangement over regions is Muster's"). So a devenv pane can sit only left or right of the laptop's panes as a whole, never below one laptop pane. Every way of placing a pane follows that rule:
- The right-click "Split on Machine" submenu splits right only, and when that machine already has panes in the tab, the new pane splits one of those rather than the pane clicked (`split_onto` in `crates/muster-seam/src/handler.rs`).
- Dragging a pane onto another machine's pane is refused (`PaneDrag.accepts` in `Sources/MusterMac/PaneDrag.swift`). Only a drop on the tab's caption in the agent list adds a machine's part.
- `muster pane new --daemon <machine> --down` puts the pane in that machine's region, not below the pane it ran from.

This reverses a recorded decision, so it needs a MIP first. architecture.md rejects an outer split tree over panes because owning one "would make it a multiplexer", and holds that the app owns no truth: a daemon's tree is what restores a tab, and a tab holding panes on two machines is written down on both daemons, with only its regions' order and widths kept by Muster. The MIP has to settle where a tree spanning machines is kept, and what it does across a daemon restart, a handoff, a machine unreachable for an hour, a window reopened while one machine is down, a pane closing on one machine, zoom, and `muster window --layout`. CLAUDE.md's "Not built" line and architecture.md change with it.
title: Arrange panes from different machines in any split, as if they were on one
